# readtheplan

> Independently verify AI-generated infrastructure changes before they execute.

readtheplan is a free, MIT-licensed, deterministic local gate. Its primary
workflow accepts Terraform/OpenTofu plan JSON, classifies individual findings
as safe, review, dangerous, or irreversible, and returns an aggregate proceed,
warn, or block decision before merge or apply.

The generator is not the approver. A coding agent may propose HCL, but
Terraform/OpenTofu must produce the structured plan and readtheplan evaluates
that artifact separately. readtheplan does not infer an agent's intent, review
arbitrary chat, run Terraform, refresh state, contact providers, or apply
infrastructure.

Additional local adapters cover other structured infrastructure, CI/CD, policy,
configuration-management, and observability artifacts. They are secondary to
the initial Terraform/OpenTofu gate and are documented in the adapter guide.
Adapters analyze source or structured exports without executing playbooks,
pipelines, templates, recipes, plugins, or infrastructure commands.

Six optional catalogs can add SOC 2, ISO 27001, HIPAA, PCI DSS, FedRAMP
Moderate, and HITRUST review context. Those annotations do not certify control
satisfaction.

Local MCP clients can request the same deterministic gate. `MCP_ROOT` confines
repository candidates, and accepted bytes are analyzed from an isolated
snapshot. The surrounding CI or agent workflow—not readtheplan—enforces the
decision.

Every product feature is free. There is no paid tier, enterprise tier, trial,
product account, or hosted raw-plan upload workflow.

- Source and issues: https://github.com/readtheplan/readtheplan

## Data boundary

Local tools process infrastructure artifacts on the user's machine or CI runner.
The optional website chat is separate, sends chat messages to DeepSeek, and must
not be used for secrets or raw infrastructure plans.

## Content use

Search indexing and live AI retrieval with attribution are welcome. Permission to
use this site's content for model training is not granted by the site's published
Content-Signal directive.
